extracted.intended_audience: rOpenSci package authors, reviewers, and editors (R package developers participating in onboarding)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for rOpenSci's package 'onboarding' peer-review process — covering packaging and reviewing guides, automated checks, timing and scope of review, reviewer recognition, and workflow improvements. Intended to inform both authors submitting R packages and reviewers/editors conducting reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfaction with onboarding
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall satisfaction with the onboarding (package review) process as a baseline metric to track year-to-year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to monitor whether improvements maintain or increase participant satisfaction as the program grows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging guide organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and organization of the packaging guide provided to authors (currently a collection of markdown files).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors suggested converting the collection of markdown files into a bookdown website for easier navigation; rOpenSci is porting docs into a common bookdown book to address this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing guide structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity and structure of the reviewing guide provided to reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents requested greater structure, more concrete advice and examples on how to approach review, and clearer expectations; rOpenSci plans to fold suggestions into the unified bookdown guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation between code and UI reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit distinction in guidance and practice between reviewing code (functional aspects) and reviewing user interface/UX elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers suggested separating these concerns in the guide to provide clearer, targeted review workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice and examples on how to approach review
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of practical advice, step-by-step processes, and exemplar reviews for reviewers to learn how to perform reviews effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blog mentions incorporating related posts from the rOpenSci blog into the new guide to provide concrete examples and approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on expectations for timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear expectations for review and revision turnaround times for both authors and reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers wanted better guidance on timelines; rOpenSci aims to include this in the improved guide and in reviewer onboarding so authors know expected lags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration between multiple reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and processes for how multiple reviewers should coordinate, divide work, and interact during a package review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents asked for clearer advice on collaboration; the new guide will address coordination and expectations among multiple reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate timing to submit (early vs mature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of when a package should be submitted for review: early-in-development versus mature (e.g., CRAN) stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade-offs: early submission allows design/usability feedback but is hard to review when incomplete; mature packages may be unable to accept breaking suggestions. No submission requirement changes planned; authors of early-stage packages are encouraged to solicit early input on the forum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of review by package maturity (short vs detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different review scopes depending on package maturity: short lightweight reviews for early-stage packages and detailed reviews for mature packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestion: provide short (<1 hour) reviews for early-stage packages and reserve detailed reviews for mature packages — rOpenSci is concerned about added reviewer workload from multi-step processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinded vs open review and reviewer objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether reviews are fully open or single-blinded to protect reviewers and encourage critical feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some respondents suggested a single-blinded system to allow reviewers, especially early-career, to provide critical comments without fear of retaliation; this weighs against openness/transparency values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-running automated checks before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should run automated quality checks (goodpractice) before submitting to reduce noise and reviewer effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents suggested adding explicit instruction that authors pre-run goodpractice and resolve or annotate results before submission; rOpenSci will add this to the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on which automated check outputs can be ignored
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear documentation about which automated check results are actionable and which can be safely ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors asked for better guidance on which outputs to ignore; rOpenSci will provide guidance and align goodpractice checks with the packaging guide to reduce false positives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customization and specialization of automated checks (rOpenSci goodpractice set)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a specialized set of rOpenSci goodpractice checks that align with the packaging guide and allow custom/ignored checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: goodpractice allows ignoring/adding custom checks. rOpenSci aims to develop a specialized rOpenSci checks set and improve goodpractice documentation; Mango Solutions is improving the package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic running of checks on submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated execution of quality checks when a package is submitted, to streamline editor and reviewer workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: rOpenSci hopes to have checks run automatically upon submission, reducing effort for both authors and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer recognition and metadata (MARC author type)
rubrics_metrics.description: How reviewers are acknowledged in package metadata (e.g., recognizing reviewers as MARC author type in DESCRIPTION files).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors requested guidance on acknowledging reviewers; rOpenSci enabled reviewer recognition via MARC author type and linked to a previous blog post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer sign-up and matching process
rubrics_metrics.description: Ease and effectiveness of the reviewer sign-up form and the editor's ability to match reviewers to submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: rOpenSci plans a new reviewer sign-up form to make it easier for editors to match reviewers to submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workload/time required for package review
rubrics_metrics.description: The time investment required to perform a package review (review burden).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey respondents reported package review is quite time consuming; this informs discussions about scope, potential short reviews, and tooling to reduce effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing ongoing revisions during submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to track and keep up with package revisions that happen while the submission is under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents found keeping up with ongoing revisions challenging; process and tooling improvements may help manage ongoing changes during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lag time between review and revision
rubrics_metrics.description: The duration between when reviewers give feedback and when authors submit revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long time lags were reported as a challenge; clearer timeline expectations and workflow changes aim to reduce this lag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value outcomes of review (networking, learning, visibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative benefits of participating: opportunity to network and share ideas, openness/transparency, learning about software design and package development, improved coding skills, two thorough code reviews, collegial and non-adversarial interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors reported blog posts after acceptance increased package visibility; these qualitative values are part of assessing the success of onboarding beyond strict quality metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to submit to JOSS (publication pathway)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may optionally submit their package to the Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS) for publication as part of or after onboarding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an offered pathway that adds value/visibility for authors and can be part of the onboarding outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraging early community feedback via forum
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that early-development packages open forum discussions to solicit early input prior to formal review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: rOpenSci suggests authors of early-development packages use the community forum to get feedback and reduce friction when formally submitting.
